paragraph: The ICT ministry, MINTTICS, [runs a public consultation portal](<https://consultapublica.minttics.gov.ao/>) for draft sector documents. In April 2025 the regulator INACOM reported that [the ministry's draft cybersecurity laws were open for comment](<https://inacom.gov.ao/2025/04/15/sessao-tematica-aborda-programa-de-desenvolvimento-e-expansao-das-telecomunicacoes-e-tecnologias-de-informacao/>) on the same portal and by email. In the last twelve months, in August 2026, the portal [carried the draft law on artificial intelligence](<https://consultapublica.minttics.gov.ao/>), showing 18 contributions from companies, 18 from specialists and 5 from the general public. In May 2026 the institute IMA [put the draft Digital Government Law on the public consultations portal](<https://ima.gov.ao/web/noticias/ima-promove-sessao-de-consulta-publica-sobre-o-anteprojecto-de-lei-do-governo-digital>). No source found since October 2023 says the government published what it was told online. Operating would need published comments, a report or an answer.

In April 2025 the Open Government Partnership [reported that the BousProB application](<https://www.opengovpartnership.org/stories/co-creation-in-action-how-benin-is-making-budgets-work-for-people/>) lets citizens in Benin follow the stages of the budget process and comment on them. The application belongs to an Open Budget Hub run by the budget directorate. The hub opens 13 of the 17 stages of the budget process to civil society. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says a portal takes comments online on more than one draft. Establishing would need a consultation portal or online platform open to the public for more than one draft.

In June 2025 a notice [put the draft Cybersecurity Bill on the website of BOCRA](<https://www.bocra.org.bw/sites/default/files/sites/default/files/documents/Preamble_to_the_Cybersecurity_Bill_Revised.pdf>), the communications regulator. Written comments went to the ministry by email, by 23 June 2025. In the last twelve months, in December 2025, the energy regulator BERA [posted a consultation paper on the power utility's 2026-27 tariff application](<https://www.bera.co.bw/downloads/Electricity/BPC%202026-27%20Tariff%20Application%20-%20Public%20Notice/BERA%2028X5%20KO.pdf>). It asked the public for written comments by email by 30 January 2026. No source found since October 2023 says a portal takes comments online on more than one draft. Establishing would need a consultation portal or online platform open to the public for more than one draft.

From 6 July to 6 August 2026 the telecoms regulator, ARTCI, [ran a public consultation on draft net-neutrality guidelines](<https://artci.ci/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/Consultation-publique_NEUTRALITE-DU-NET-Contribution_-MOOV-AFRICA-CI.pdf>). The consultation document was on its website, and replies were taken by email. In the last twelve months, in September 2026, ARTCI [published the operators' replies to the consultation on its website](<https://artci.ci/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/Consultation-publique_NEUTRALITE-DU-NET-Contribution_-MOOV-AFRICA-CI.pdf>). No source found since October 2023 names a consultation portal in service, and none shows one taking comments on more than one draft. Establishing would need a consultation portal or online platform open to the public for more than one draft.

The Ministry of Posts and Telecommunications put out for consultation, under the PATNUC project, [a 13-page draft implementing decree for the data protection authority, online on its website](<https://obs-cc.org/gouvernance-donnees-afrique-centrale-apdp/>). In the last twelve months, in September 2026, the observatory OBS-CC reported that consultation. No source found since October 2023 says a portal is in service. None says comments were published. None says a rule requires drafts online. Establishing would need a consultation portal or online platform open to the public for more than one draft.

From 3 March to 2 April 2025 the telecoms regulator, ARPTC, [opened a public consultation on bringing in 5G](<https://arptc.gouv.cd/app/uploads/2025/03/Questionnaire_Consultation-publique_RDC_V7_010325.pdf>). Its questionnaire of 24 questions could be downloaded from the regulator's website, and replies were sent by email. In September 2025 the Minister of Youth [launched the National Youth Consultations 2025](<https://www.xtrafrica.com/news/grace-kutino-national-youth-consultations-2025>) with an online form for young people. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says a portal takes comments online on more than one draft. Establishing would need a consultation portal or online platform open to the public for more than one draft.

[The government told the World Bank's GovTech survey in 2025](<https://datacatalog.worldbank.org/search/dataset/0037889/govtech-dataset>) that Cape Verde has a national platform for citizens to take part in policy decisions, at eparticipa.gov.cv. In June 2025 the government [put its fiscal transparency portal out to public consultation](<https://www.governo.cv/portal-da-transparencia-em-consulta-publica/>), from 27 June to 17 July 2025. In the last twelve months, in August 2026, the regulator ARME [opened a public consultation on a proposed framework for satellite communications](<https://spaceinafrica.com/2026/08/05/cape-verde-opens-public-consultation-on-new-satellite-communications-regulatory-framework/>). Submissions were open until 31 August 2026. No source found since October 2023 says the government published what it was told online. Operating would need published comments, a report or an answer.

In January 2025 the National Observatory of Civil Society [opened a digital platform for associations](<https://www.aljazairalyoum.dz/%d9%84%d8%a5%d8%ab%d8%b1%d8%a7%d8%a1-%d8%a7%d9%84%d9%85%d8%b4%d8%b1%d9%88%d8%b9-%d8%a7%d9%84%d8%aa%d9%85%d9%87%d9%8a%d8%af%d9%8a-%d9%84%d9%82%d8%a7%d9%86%d9%88%d9%86-%d8%a7%d9%84%d8%ac%d9%85%d8%b9/>) to register and give their views on the draft organic law on associations. It stayed open until 30 January 2025. In the last twelve months, in April 2026, the Ministry of Youth [launched Sawtoukoum](<https://www.dzair-tube.dz/en/algeria-launches-sawtoukoum-platform-to-channel-youth-feedback-and-complaints/>), a digital platform where young people send proposals and observations to feed policy. No source found since October 2023 says a portal takes comments online on more than one draft. Establishing would need a consultation portal or online platform open to the public for more than one draft.

In May 2025 IDSC [described the Hiwar platform](<https://www.masrtimes.com/531613>), where registered citizens comment on issues the government puts to them. It said two new issues go up every 30 days, and that month they were aviation and water quality. In the last twelve months, in January 2026, the Egyptian Tax Authority [launched a consultation platform](<https://cairoscene.com/News/Tax-Authority-Launches-Consultation-Platform-for-Businesses>). Companies and business sectors send views and proposals there before tax decisions are issued. No source found since October 2023 says the government published what it was told online. Operating would need published comments, a report or an answer.

No stage is set. In May 2025 the Ministry of Justice [launched an e-consultation portal for draft laws](<https://justice.gov.et/en/news/e-consultation-portal-launched-to-ensure-public-and-stakeholder-participation-in-the-law-making-process/>). No source found since October 2023 names a draft put to the public on it. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found says laws and policies are adopted with no public consultation. Preparing would need a named draft posted online for public comment, or an online consultation on one.

No stage is set. Nothing found since October 2023 says whether the government has asked the public for views online. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found names a draft law, policy or regulation posted online for public comment, or an online consultation or survey on one. Preparing would need a named draft posted online for public comment, or an online consultation on one.

In March 2024 a [World Bank blog](<https://blogs.worldbank.org/en/africacan/transforming-governance-in-ghana-a-new-regulatory-service-model>) said the Business Regulatory Reform unit of the Ministry of Trade and Industry runs a Public Consultation Portal. Civil society reads draft laws and regulatory proposals there, and the unit's officials review the comments and poll results. In 2021 the MSME Classification Regulation drew over 1,000 views and suggestions on it, and one was adopted in the final text. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says the government published what it was told online. Operating would need published comments, a report or an answer.

As retrieved in October 2026, the Secretariat General of the Government [keeps a web page of draft texts open for public comment](<https://sgg.gov.gn/document/textecom/1>). It listed three drafts, among them the bill revising the labour code. Each draft carries a button to read the text and another to comment on it. The page shows how many comments each has received: 2 on one draft and 9 on another. It does not show the comments. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says the government published what it was told online. Operating would need published comments, a report or an answer.

In June 2025 the Public Utilities Regulatory Authority, PURA, [posted the draft Gateway Traffic Measurement and Revenue Assurance Regulations 2025](<https://pura.gm/public-consultation-on-the-draft-gateway-traffic-measurement-and-revenue-assurance-regulations-2025/>) for comment from 3 to 17 June. Comments went by email. In the last twelve months, in April 2026, it [posted seven named draft regulatory instruments on its website](<https://pura.gm/public-consultation-guidelines-and-notice/>). It invited comments by email between 1 and 10 April. One was [the Broadcasting and Online Content Regulations, 2026](<https://pura.gm/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/Broadcasting-and-Online-Content-Regulations-2026-.pdf>). No source found since October 2023 says a portal takes comments online on more than one draft. Establishing would need a consultation portal or online platform open to the public for more than one draft.

In May 2026 the board of the telecoms regulator, ARN-TIC, [opened a public consultation on the draft Electronic Transactions Law](<https://www.odemocratagb.com/?p=57171>). The draft was on the regulator's website, and replies were taken by email for 30 days, to 28 May 2026. The regulator opened it in the last twelve months, and no earlier consultation has been found. No source found since October 2023 says a portal takes comments online on more than one draft. Establishing would need a consultation portal or online platform open to the public for more than one draft.

[The government told the World Bank's GovTech survey in 2025](<https://datacatalog.worldbank.org/search/dataset/0037889/govtech-dataset>) that Kenya has a national platform for citizen participation in policy, at publicparticipation.statelaw.go.ke. In the last twelve months, in April 2026, the Kenya National Bureau of Statistics [put the draft Statistics Bill, 2026 on its website](<https://gaa.go.ke/sites/default/files/2026-04/Kenya%20National%20Bureau%20of%20Statistics%2C%20Call%20For%20Comments%20And%20Public%20Participation%20Forums%20On%20The%20Statistics%20Bill%2C%202026.pdf>). It invited written comments by email. In May 2026 the information ministry [posted its draft National Data Governance Policy online for public comment](<https://posts.kictanet.or.ke/have-your-say-kenyas-draft-national-data-governance-policy-comments-due-5-june-2026/>), due by 5 June 2026. No source found since October 2023 says the government published what it was told online. Operating would need published comments, a report or an answer.

No stage is set. The Liberia Telecommunications Authority [published its draft quality of service regulations online in March 2021](<https://lta.gov.lr/wp-content/uploads/2024/03/Final-Report-on-QoS-Regulation-Consultation-December-4-2023-Version.pdf>). On 4 March 2024 it issued a final report on the consultation, setting out the inputs received and its decision on each. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says a named draft was posted online for public comment. Preparing would need a named draft posted online for public comment, or an online consultation on one.

No stage is set. Nothing found since October 2023 says whether the government has asked the public for views online. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found names a draft law, policy or regulation posted online for public comment, or an online consultation or survey on one. Preparing would need a named draft posted online for public comment, or an online consultation on one.

[The World Bank's GovTech survey records in 2025](<https://datacatalog.worldbank.org/search/dataset/0037889/govtech-dataset>) a national platform for citizen participation in policy decision-making in Morocco, at www.eparticipation.ma. In the last twelve months, on 16 September 2026, Aujourd'hui le Maroc reported that [draft law 62.25 on climate change and the carbon market was under public consultation](<https://aujourdhui.ma/societe/un-avant-projet-de-loi-soumis-au-sgg-le-maroc-encadre-le-marche-carbone>). The draft was on the website of the Secretariat General of the Government. No source found since October 2023 says the government published what it was told online. Operating would need published comments, a report or an answer.

The National Assembly [runs a public consultation portal](<https://parlement.mg/consultations/>) that takes citizens' contributions on bills. It lists a bill on the environment and natural resources, open from December 2025 to February 2026. In the last twelve months, the Electoral Code reform was open on the portal from 13 February to 13 March 2026, and the portal marks it closed. It also lists a consultation on the 2026 budget priorities. No source found since October 2023 says the government published what it was told online. Operating would need published comments, a report or an answer.

In April 2025 the central bank, Banco de Moçambique, posted [a draft revision of its mobile money notice](<https://www.bancomoc.mz/en/media/highlights/public-consultation-on-the-proposed-revision-of-the-notice-that-establishes-measures-for-protecting-customer-funds-received-in-exchange-for-mobile-money/>) for consultation. In June 2025 it posted [a draft revision of its complaints-handling rules](<https://www.bancomoc.mz/pt/media/noticias/consulta-p%C3%BAblica-sobre-a-proposta-de-revis%C3%A3o-do-aviso-n-%C2%BA-9-gbm-2020-de-31-de-dezembro-que-aprova-o-regulamento-de-tratamento-de-reclama%C3%A7%C3%B5es/>). In the last twelve months, in May 2026, the ICT institute INTIC [posted the first draft of the National Artificial Intelligence Strategy on its portal](<https://intic.gov.mz/consulta-publica-da-proposta-da-estrategia-nacional-de-inteligencia-artificial/>), open from 4 May to 4 June 2026. Comments went by email. No source found since October 2023 says a portal takes comments online. Establishing would need a consultation portal or online platform open to the public for more than one draft.

No stage is set. In May 2024 the human rights commissariat [launched the Space Plateforme](<https://ami.mr/fr/archives/247074>) for dialogue on public policy between government, civil society and partners. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 names a draft or policy put to the public online. Preparing would need a named draft posted online for public comment, or an online consultation on one.

On 10 April 2025 the government [launched a public consultation on a draft report on children's online safety](<https://www.govmu.org/EN/newsgov/SitePages/Government-launches-public-consultation-to-beef-up-online-safety-of-children.aspx>). The draft was on the ministry's website, and views were taken by email or through the MAIA+ chatbot. In the last twelve months, in 2026, the National Agency for Drug Control [ran a submission portal for cannabis policy reform](<https://consultations.nadc.mu/>) that collected public comments and proposals online until 21 June 2026. Its working group [opened the platform on 29 May 2026](<https://topfm.mu/consultation-publique-sur-la-reforme-de-la-politique-du-cannabis-la-plateforme-en-ligne-est-ouverte>). No source found since October 2023 says a portal takes comments online on more than one draft. Establishing would need a consultation portal or online platform open to the public for more than one draft.

In February 2024 the Ministry of Information and Digitalization, through the regulator MACRA, [invited the public to a hybrid consultation meeting](<https://digmap.pppc.mw/invitation-to-a-hybrid-public-stakeholder-consultation-meeting-on-the-electronic-transactions-and-cyber-security-act-etca-regulations-bingu-international-conference-centre-bicc-in-lilong/>) on three named draft regulations under the Electronic Transactions and Cyber Security Act. People could attend in Lilongwe or online through Teams. The drafts were linked from the invitation by QR code. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says a portal takes comments online on more than one draft. Establishing would need a consultation portal or online platform open to the public for more than one draft.

In August 2026 the Namibia Green Hydrogen Programme, acting for the government, [opened a two-week window for comments online](<https://namibiabusinessreview.com/namibia-seeks-public-input-to-unlock-n4-1bn-green-fund/>) on the draft Sectoral Transformation Investment Plan. Comments were taken at gh2namibia.com. The plan is meant to unlock a green fund of N$4.1 billion. In the last twelve months this is the one online consultation found, and none earlier has been found. No source found since October 2023 says a portal takes comments online on more than one draft. Establishing would need a consultation portal or online platform open to the public for more than one draft.

In February 2025 the website of the national conference on refoundation, the Assises Nationales pour la Refondation, [invited the public to leave proposals as comments](<https://www.assises-nationales.ne/>). The calls came from two of its commissions, one on justice and human rights and one on international geopolitics and the environment. Members of the public could post their proposals beneath each call. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says a portal takes comments online on more than one draft. Establishing would need a consultation portal or online platform open to the public for more than one draft.

On 19 June 2026 the Nigerian Communications Commission and a joint committee [issued a consultation paper on zero-rated access to educational platforms](<https://www.ncc.gov.ng/sites/default/files/2026-06/Consultation-Paper-on-Zero-Rated-Access-to-Educational-Platforms.pdf>). It was open for comment to 9 July 2026. In the last twelve months, on 3 August 2026, the Presidential Working Group on the National Policing Bill [opened a portal for the public to propose changes to the bill](<https://businessday.ng/news/article/state-police-bill-fg-unveils-timelines-opens-link-for-public-engagements/>). In August 2026 the Federal Ministry of Finance [invited proposals for the Finance Bill 2027](<https://naltf.gov.ng/finance-bill-2027-fg-seeks-inputs-from-public/>) online or by email. It closed on 11 September 2026. No source found since October 2023 says a portal takes comments online on more than one draft. Establishing would need a consultation portal or online platform open to the public for more than one draft.

In March 2025 the Capital Market Authority and the National Bank of Rwanda [published the draft law regulating virtual assets business](<https://bitcoinke.io/2025/03/rwanda-invites-public-comments-on-virtual-assets-draft-law/>). Comments went by email, and a consultation was held on Zoom on 17 March 2025. In the last twelve months, in February 2026, the Capital Market Authority [invited the public to comment on a draft regulation](<https://www.cma.rw/news-publications/press-center/call-for-public-comments-on-the-draft-regulation-governing-intermediary-service-platform-operators>) governing operators of intermediary service platforms. The draft was on its website, with comments by email by 24 February 2026. No source found since October 2023 says a portal takes comments online on more than one draft. Establishing would need a consultation portal or online platform open to the public for more than one draft.

[The digital ministry's consultation on the 2025-2035 digital strategy drew more than 700 contributions on Jubbanti](<https://letechobservateur.sn/cloture-de-la-consultation-publique-pour-la-strategie-numerique-du-senegal-2025-2035-un-pas-vers-une-transformation-digitaleinclusive/>), after opening on 25 July 2024. [The World Bank's GovTech record lists the Jubbanti platform](<https://datacatalog.worldbank.org/search/dataset/0037889/govtech-dataset>), as at 2025, as a national platform for citizen participation in policy. In the last twelve months, in March 2026, the telecoms regulator ARTP [launched a public consultation on deploying and sharing FTTx fibre networks](<https://artp.sn/partage-infrastructures/fttx>). In August 2026 it published a synthesis report of the twenty-one contributions on its website. No source found since October 2023 says a rule requires drafts to be put online for public comment. Mature would need an online consultation held because a rule requires drafts online.

On 17 March 2024 the Speaker of the Lower House, Madobe, [launched a Digital Platform for Public Consultations](<https://radiodalsan.com/2024/03/18/speaker-madobe-launches-digital-platform-for-public-consultations-on-constitutional-review/>) on the proposed constitutional amendments. The Independent Constitutional Review and Implementation Commission built it to gather citizens' views. In July 2023 the National Communications Authority [invited comments by email on its draft strategic plan for 2023-2027](<https://nca.gov.so/strategic-plan-2023-207/>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says a portal takes comments online on more than one draft. Establishing would need a consultation portal or online platform open to the public for more than one draft.

In September 2025 the regulator AGER [posted the National Cybersecurity Strategy 2024-2028 and its action plan on its website](<https://www.ager.st/index.php/pt/actualidades/19-annonces/106-estrategia-nacional-de-ciberseguranca-de-sao-tome-e-principe>) for public consultation. Contributions were to be sent within 30 days, and the notice gave telephone and email contacts for them. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says a portal takes comments online on more than one draft. Establishing would need a consultation portal or online platform open to the public for more than one draft.

In November 2024 the Eswatini Communications Commission [posted a proposed decision to retire 2G and 3G networks](<https://web.archive.org/web/20241110181421/https://www.esccom.org.sz/publications/notices/docs/Notice%2012%20Proposed%20Decision%20to%20Retire%20Legacy%20Networks.pdf>). Comments went by email by 9 December 2024. In July 2025 it [posted a proposed broadcasting licence fee schedule on its website](<https://www.esccom.org.sz/publications/notices/docs/Notice%207%20PROPOSED%20DECISION%20TO%20ISSUE%20BROADCASTING%20FEES%20SCHEDULE.pdf>) and invited written comments by email until 11 August 2025. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says a portal takes comments online on more than one draft. Establishing would need a consultation portal or online platform open to the public for more than one draft.

[In February 2024 the Central Bank of Seychelles invited the public to comment on proposed amendments to its payment system licensing regulations](<https://www.nation.sc/articles/21119/cbs-opens-public-consultation-on-proposed-amendments-to-the-national-payment-system-licensing-and-authorisation-regulations-2014>). The consultation paper was posted on the bank's website, with comments by email until 29 February 2024. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No standing online consultation portal has been found. Nor has a report of comments received, or a rule requiring online consultation. Establishing would need a consultation portal or online platform open to the public for more than one draft.

In January 2024 Prime Minister Succès Masra [asked Chadians on social media](<https://www.rfi.fr/fr/afrique/20240116-tchad-le-premier-ministre-succ%C3%A8s-masra-consulte-les-tchadiens-sur-les-r%C3%A9seaux-sociaux>) what they expected of his government. He also asked for the three sectors they would make priorities, ahead of the government programme he was to present on 18 January 2024. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says a portal takes comments online on more than one draft. Establishing would need a consultation portal or online platform open to the public for more than one draft.

No stage is set. In January 2025 the government [launched an online suggestion box](<https://ledefenseurinfo.tg/boite-a-suggestions-une-plateforme-pour-impliquer-les-citoyens-dans-la-securite/>) where citizens send ideas on national security. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 names a draft law or policy put to the public online. Preparing would need a named draft posted online for public comment, or an online consultation on one.

[Tunisia's government told the World Bank's GovTech survey in 2025](<https://datacatalog.worldbank.org/search/dataset/0037889/govtech-dataset>) that e-people.gov.tn is a national platform allowing citizens to take part in policy decision-making. [From 19 March to 20 April 2025 the E-Government Unit ran an online public survey on a national open data strategy](<http://www.ogptunisie.gov.tn/fr/index.php/2025/03/19/lancement-de-lenquete-publique-en-ligne-sur-lelaboration-de-la-strategie-nationale-de-promotion-de-louverture-et-de-la-reutilisation-des-donnees-publiques/>). In the last twelve months, in March 2026, the telecoms regulator, INT, [opened a second consultation on sharing fibre access infrastructure](<https://www.intt.tn/fr/index.php?actu=1060&typeactu=89>). It ran to 2 April 2026, with replies by email. No source found since October 2023 says the government published what it was told online. Operating would need published comments, a report or an answer.

In June 2025 the Ministry of Finance [said its Maoni Portal is open to the public](<https://www.therespondents.co.tz/2025/06/tanzania-invites-public-input-on-tax.html>). It said each December it opens a window on the portal for views on improving the tax system, and invited the public to send views on tax policy through it. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says a portal takes comments online on more than one draft. Establishing would need a consultation portal or online platform open to the public for more than one draft.

[In September 2025 the Information Regulator published draft regulations on health and sex-life data](<https://www.gov.za/sites/default/files/gcis_document/202509/53426gon6673.pdf>), with written comments due by 10 October 2025. In the last twelve months, Home Affairs [published the draft revised white paper on citizenship, immigration and refugee protection for public comment](<https://www.gov.za/news/speeches/minister-leon-schreiber-invites-public-comment-draft-revised-white-paper-citizenship>). The draft was on its website from 12 December 2025 to 31 January 2026. Written comments went by email. The Reserve Bank [lists a 2026 draft directive on payments for offshore merchants](<https://www.resbank.co.za/en/home/what-we-do/payments-and-settlements/regulation>). Comments were due on 17 July 2026. No source found since October 2023 says a portal takes comments online on more than one draft. Establishing would need a consultation portal or online platform open to the public for more than one draft.

In the last twelve months, on 21 October 2026, the telecoms regulator, ZICTA, [put its draft revised type approval guidelines on its website for comment](<https://ib-lenhardt.com/media/pages/news/consultation-on-draft-revised-type-approval-guidelines/3220b471e8-1792662126/public-notice-draft-revised-type-approval-guidelines_20102026.pdf>). Comments are taken through an online form until 20 November 2026. In August 2026 the Zambia Bureau of Standards [posted draft standards for comment on its website](<https://www.zabs.org.zm/standards-development>), with 37 drafts up for review. Comments on those are made on the bureau's enquiry form. No source found since October 2023 shows a portal taking comments online on more than one draft. Establishing would need a consultation portal or online platform open to the public for more than one draft.

No stage is set. In 2026 [Mutare City Council ran its budget consultations through a WhatsApp chatbot and an online platform](<https://www.clgf.org.uk/whats-new/news/cscn-peer-learning-clinic-highlights-mutares-digital-transformation-journey-to-strengthen-municipal-finance/>). In the last twelve months, that is the only online consultation found, and it is a city council's. Nothing found says a ministry, parliament or regulator has asked the public for views online. Preparing would need a named draft posted online for public comment, or an online consultation on one.
